_comment: Navigation probes: does the route this repository documents still lead to the answer?
These are not content tests and not behaviour probes -- they prove FINDABILITY, which is
the whole reason a prebuilt index is worth shipping.
`reject` matters as much as `expect`. Several of the things this repository must get right
are absences: that the hosted document does not carry a builder method, that a type nobody
can name is not filed beside one they can. A positive-only probe cannot check any of them.
NOTE the name. In the earliest repositories in this family `probes.json` meant THIS, and in
the later ones it means executed behaviour probes. Both exist here, so they are named apart.

probes.question: Does the index carry the builder methods no published artifact documents?
Does every undocumented method say how to reach it?
Is the doc(hidden) pair kept distinct from the undocumented-but-supported pair?
Is InstrumentedExec filed as internal rather than as something to recommend?
Is the name that appears in neither rustdoc document recorded rather than dropped?
Does the macro table carry the invocation grammar?
Does the rules family require state:?
Does the span table say which fields the node span carries?
Is datafusion.preview attributed to the option that produces it?
Are node-dependent metric fields kept out of the option column?
Does the compatibility table carry the opentelemetry pairs?
Does compatibility distinguish a historical pattern from a contract?
Does the span catalog warn that the target is the caller's crate?
Does the span catalog refuse to claim the metric vocabulary is complete?
Is the malformed upstream snapshot disclosed rather than silently repaired?
Does every seam page carry its refusal section?
probes.expect: ## What this seam cannot tell you

probes.question: Does the boundary seam say DataFusion is out of scope?
Does the router name the source a reader was about to trust?
Does the negative-space catalog give an alternative for InstrumentedExec?
Does the crate map record the five rustdoc format versions docs.rs served?
Are only subject execution macros counted in the execution family?
Can a library target also contain planning telemetry?
Is public EOF behavior tied to the resolved stream adapter?
probes.expect: reaching EOF closes spans while the public stream adapters
